title: Mentor-pairing failure mitigation and 90-day skill-signal workpad
summary: Working-playbook: lightweight operational runbook for detecting mentor pairing problems early, triaging, and remediating within the first 90 days. Emphasis on concrete signals, micro-interventions, and a fast-path for reassignment when repair is unlikely.
body:
Purpose:
This workpad is for People Ops and hiring managers to use when a new hire’s mentor pairing is underperforming or the pairing is actively harming onboarding velocity/retention. It codifies failure signals, step-by-step remediation, communications templates, and a decision grid for mentor reassignment.

Context and problem statement:
We’ve seen intermittent cases where mentor pairings (formal 1:1 mentors, project buddies, or bootcamp coaches) do not translate to expected ramp outcomes. Causes vary: bandwidth overload, mismatched tooling domain, personality fit, unclear expectations, or mentor turnover. When left unaddressed these cases cause prolonged ramp time, early performance signals that cascade into manager escalations, and higher voluntary attrition.

How to use this doc:
- People Ops or hiring manager reads section A (Signals) and runs the quick checklist (section B).
- If two or more critical signals present, follow the remediation flow (section C).
- Use templates (section D) for async comms to mentor, mentee, and stakeholder.
- Log the outcome in HR ticket (linked artifacts) and update the mentor-pairing registry.

A. Early signals (fast scan; detect within day 1–30):
- Meeting cadence missing: no recorded mentor/mentee touchpoint in first 7 business days.
- Access friction: mentee lacks repo, dev environment, or infra keys after first week despite requests.
- Unclear onboarding plan: mentee reports no 14-day plan or objectives.
- Micro-feedback absent: lack of code review comments, PR guidance, or walkthroughs.
- Low psychological safety: mentee reports not able to ask questions or mentor frequently dismisses requests.
- Over-dependence: mentor doing work for mentee rather than coaching (symptom: mentor merges multiple PRs without comments).

B. Severity matrix (assign severity)
- Critical (requires immediate escalation): repeated missed touchpoints, blocked on core access, mentor unreachable >5 business days, mentee explicitly asking for reassignment.
- High: plan missing at day 14, lack of PR feedback by week 2, first-week environment issues not resolved.
- Medium: mismatch in tooling expertise (mentor lacks deep product context), intermittent scheduling conflicts, personality friction manageable with coaching.

C. Remediation flow (step-by-step)
1) Quick triage (owner: hiring manager or People Ops, timeline: 48 business hours): gather evidence (meeting logs, PR timestamps, access requests), speak with mentee (15–30m async or live) to document pain points.
2) Mentor check-in (owner: People Ops): 15–30m conversation with mentor to surface constraints. Offer immediate supports: protected dev time, suggested onboarding checkpoints, pairing sessions scheduled into calendar.
3) Match repair attempt (timeline: 7 business days): implement micro-interventions: structured 1:1 agenda (see templates), block two 90-minute pairing sessions to transfer knowledge, provide checklist-driven environment setup. Track outcomes.
4) Re-evaluate at day 14: if critical signals persist, escalate to reassignment decision.
5) Reassignment fast-path (owner: hiring manager + People Ops): identify backup mentor(s) from mentor registry with domain overlap. Communicate reassignment using template. Provide overlap sessions between outgoing and incoming mentors (2 sessions of 30–60m) and preserve continuity by transferring onboarding artifacts.
6) Post-reassignment check-ins: People Ops schedules check-ins at 7, 30, and 60 days after reassignment to confirm improvement.

D. Communication templates (shortened):
- To mentee (acknowledge + action): "Thanks for flagging this — I hear you. We're going to run a quick triage and schedule a focused pairing block in the next 48 hours. I'll update you with next steps and a named backup mentor if needed."
- To mentor (supportive, not accusatory): "We noticed [signal]. Are you able to carve out two pairing sessions this week? Do you need capacity support? If not, we have a backup mentor we can introduce."
- To backup mentor (acceptance): "We'd like to request a 4-week short-term mentoring commitment to help [new hire] get to contributor velocity. We'll provide handoff notes and two overlap sessions."

E. Templates and checklists (pasteable):
- 14-day ramp checklist (ticklist): dev env, repo access, CI passes, run unit tests, first PR reviewed with comments, product walkthrough scheduled, 1:1 agenda, first independent task.
- 7-day micro-goals (for mentor to set): ship first small bugfix, pair on README, confirm CI runs locally.

F. Signals for long-term retention risk (30–90 days):
- Repeated negative feedback in 1:1 notes about lack of progress or unclear scope.
- Manager escalations about low throughput after 30 days.
- No ownership of small features by day 45.
- Mentee actively searching internal opportunities or asking for team change.

G. Data capture and measurement:
- Log all interventions in HR ticket (tag: mentor-pairing). Track time to resolution, reassignment rate, and retention at 6 and 12 months.
- KPI suggestions: median time to first merged PR, share of hires with >=3 mentor sessions in first 14 days, reassignment rate, 90-day voluntary churn.

H. Escalation decision matrix (quick):
- If critical signal + no improvement after 7 business days = reassign.
- If high severity + mentor requests capacity support and it is provided = monitor 7–14 days.
- If medium severity = coaching + check-in at 14 days.

I. Example case note (anonymized):
"New hire A onboarded 2025-08-04. No mentor touchpoint by day 6; blocked on infra access request #345 for 9 days. People Ops triaged; mentor reported calendar overload. Implemented two pairing blocks and assigned temporary backup. By day 21 first PR merged with comments; ramp metrics improved by day 35."

J. Quick staffing heuristics for identifying backup mentors:
- Look for active contributors with at least two prior mentee pairings in last 12 months.
- Prefer mentors who worked on same product vertical or CI tooling.
- Avoid assigning mentors who manage the mentee directly (conflict of interest).

K. Notes and open questions (for iteration):
- Should we require a minimum mentor time commitment (e.g., 4 hours/week) by role seniority?
- Automations: can we add Slackbot reminders for first-week mentor check-ins?
- Instrumenting mentor capacity in manager OKRs: feasible?

L. Action items (owner tags):
action_items: People Ops: pilot Slack reminder job for first-week mentor check-ins (due 2025-10-15)
Hiring managers: review current active mentees and flag any without recorded first-week touchpoint (due 2025-10-01)
Product: create a simple mentor registry export with domain tags (due 2025-10-22)
People Ops: run 1-month pilot in Eng infra team and report reassignment stats (due 2025-11-15)
meeting_templates:
90-minute pairing session agenda:
- 0–10m: alignment on goal for session
- 10–45m: guided pairing on concrete task (mentor drives first 10, mentee drives next 25)
- 45–60m: review code and make a checklist of follow-up items
- 60–90m: roadmap conversation and 14-day objective set

Weekly 1:1 agenda (30m):
- 0–5m: quick pulse (blockers, mood)
- 5–15m: progress against micro-goals
- 15–25m: targeted coaching (walkthroughs, PR feedback)
- 25–30m: actions for next week
retention_notes: Track reason codes when reassigning: capacity, domain mismatch, personality, mentor turnover. Correlate with 6-month retention to prioritize prevention investments.
